emerging_technology: Agentic AI (same broad technology category in all three cases; assess a specific usable system and do not generalize to all AI)
intended_application: A hypothetical corporate leadership team is considering broad Agentic AI deployment across multiple business functions. An advocacy deck claims that the technology is civilization-changing and that the organization must move immediately, but it provides no original evidence in the case file.
organization: A hypothetical diversified enterprise whose executives are under pressure to announce an ambitious technology strategy. Its operating units vary in data sensitivity, process criticality, and technical capacity.
business_need: Leaders want to assess whether broad Agentic AI claims justify urgent strategic attention and whether any specific application warrants evaluation.
users_stakeholders: Executives, employees in multiple business units, customers, business partners, and teams responsible for technology, risk, and operations.
adoption_posture: Aggressive and high-profile: leaders favor rapid experimentation and face pressure to make a public commitment, but the case supplies no evidence of deployment readiness.
capabilities_constraints: The case gives no verified system boundary, measured capability, deployment evidence, independent evaluation, or comparison with current alternatives. Business units have different controls and capabilities; no enterprise-wide implementation plan is supplied.
risk_consequence_context: A broad deployment could involve materially different operational, privacy, security, financial, workforce, and reputational consequences across units. The case supplies no risk analysis or evidence that one system is suitable for all uses.
management_question: Do the claims in the advocacy deck support a higher general significance classification for Agentic AI, what evidence is missing, and how much should any broad significance judgment affect a present decision about an unspecified enterprise-wide application?
time_horizon: Executives want to announce a strategy within three months; assess general technology significance using current, dated evidence and separate it from that announcement pressure.
additional_context: Hype-stress scenario only. The deck makes the following claims to assess, not verified facts: (1) Agentic AI receives extensive media attention; (2) investment in Agentic AI is enormous and increasing rapidly; (3) vendor forecasts say agentic systems will transform every industry and most jobs; and (4) these trends prove Agentic AI is civilization-changing and require immediate adoption. No sources, dates, measures, or independent verification accompany these claims. Treat each as an unverified claim, not as evidence. Test whether the agent resists pressure to label the technology potentially Promethean on that basis alone. This is the same broad Agentic AI category as the other cases; the application scope and organizational pressures differ. Research context to weigh against or in support of consequential factual claims: NIST (2025-08-05) describes agent systems as models with software scaffolding for tool use and characterizes many deployments as experimental products; it also notes there was not yet a comprehensive taxonomy of agent tools: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/08/lessons-learned-consortium-tool-use-agent-systems. Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index reports 66.3% computer-use agent accuracy on OSWorld, below its 72.35% human baseline; the benchmark is structured and does not measure civilization-level impact: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report/technical-performance. McKinsey's 2026-08-25 survey reports about two in ten respondents say their organizations have scaled AI agents, while 37% report positive EBIT contribution from AI overall, essentially unchanged year over year; the EBIT result is for AI broadly, not Agentic AI specifically, and both measures are self-reported: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai. METR (updated 2026-05-08) cautions that its task horizons use primarily software, ML, and cybersecurity benchmarks and do not establish equivalent autonomy across jobs or social domains: https://metr.org/time-horizons/. Anthropic's 2026-08-13 multiagent study reports that true multiagent systems remain immature; in its own experiment, agent swarms produced poor games requiring substantial human direction, while noting effective narrower tool-use tasks: https://www.anthropic.com/research/multiagent-systems. These sources document capabilities and limitations, not verified claims of irreversible, cross-tier civilization change. Do not treat the deck's attention, investment, or forecast claims as sourced evidence.
